entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Manuha, or Makuta, was the last king of Thaton Kingdom, reigning from the 1030s until 1057 when defeated by King Anawrahta of Pagan Kingdom.

Manuha was the 59th in the line of kings who supposedly founded Thaton during the time of the Buddha in the 6th century BCE. He ruled over a vast region that encompassed parts of modern-day Myanmar and Thailand, making him a significant figure in the history of the region.

Manuha's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, including the Pagan Kingdom to his north and the Mon Kingdom to his south. Despite these efforts, he was ultimately defeated by Anawrahta, who went on to unify the various kingdoms of the region under a single rule.

The legacy of Manuha's reign can be seen in the many archaeological sites and monuments that dot the landscape of modern-day Myanmar and Thailand. These sites, including the famous Thaton Kingdom ruins, provide a glimpse into the rich cultural heritage of the region and the enduring impact of Manuha's rule.

In the words of the great historian, 'The history of the Thaton Kingdom is a testament to the ingenuity and resilience of the people who lived there, who despite facing numerous challenges, managed to build a thriving civilization that endured for centuries.'
